After its 1998 sale, he founded Hutchings Automotive Products and continued manufacturing fluid-carrying systems.

long_biography.plain_text:
By his thirties, James Lealand “Jack” Hutchings was virtually blind from a congenital optic-nerve disorder. Born in Pontiac, Michigan, he had grown up in a troubled household and was legally blind by sixteen. A gifted singer, he won a music scholarship but chose marriage and work at S. S. Kresge. Financial hardship eventually pushed him to rely on his mechanical ability and start a garage business with $25 and a few pieces of equipment.

That venture became S&H Fabricating & Engineering in 1968, supplying automotive air-conditioning assemblies and deriving most of its work from General Motors. Hutchings credited specialist managers with helping the company scale while he judged shifts in the vehicle market. After S&H was sold in 1998, he founded Hutchings Automotive Products. The second company manufactured tube, hose and fluid-carrying systems for automotive powertrain and cooling applications.
